rrel-01-c2.text: Fourth Lateran Council (1215). Fourth Lateran Council: Canons, Canon 62. Fordham University Medieval Sourcebook.
rrel-01-c2.quote: In the future old relics may not be exhibited outside of a vessel or exposed for sale.
rrel-01-c2.claim: The Fourth Lateran Council (1215) banned the sale of relics and their display outside a reliquary

rrel-01-c2.text: Holy See (1983). Code of Canon Law, Book IV, Title IV, canon 1190. Vatican (vatican.va).
rrel-01-c2.quote: It is absolutely forbidden to sell sacred relics.
rrel-01-c2.claim: the current Code of Canon Law (1983) states that selling sacred relics is "absolutely forbidden."

rrel-01-c3.text: Second Council of Nicaea (787). Canons of the Seventh Ecumenical Council, Canon VII, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, Vol. 14. New Advent (Schaff and Wace, eds.).
rrel-01-c3.quote: if any bishop from this time forward is found consecrating a temple without holy relics
rrel-01-c3.claim: The Second Council of Nicaea (787), called mainly to restore the veneration of icons after Byzantine iconoclasm, ruled in its seventh canon that churches consecrated without relics must have them deposited

rrel-01-c3.text: Sister Vajira and Francis Story (trans.) (1998). Maha-parinibbana Sutta: Last Days of the Buddha (DN 16). Access to Insight (Buddhist Publication Society).
rrel-01-c3.quote: So it came about that there were eight stupas for the relics, a ninth for the urn, and a tenth for the ashes.
rrel-01-c3.claim: A Brahmin named Dona divided the bones into eight shares. He kept the measuring vessel, and a latecomer clan received the embers, making ten monuments in all.
